He played [[college basketball]] for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]]. ==Early life== Richard Warner Saunders was born on September 19, 2001, in [[Riverton, Utah]], to Lisa and Rich Saunders.{{Cite web |title=Richie Saunders – Men's Basketball 2025-2026 |url=https://byucougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/player/richie-saunders |url-status=live |access-date=June 26, 2026 |publisher=[[BYU Cougars]] |language=en-US |via=[[Brigham Young University]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317012111/https://byucougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/player/richie-saunders|archive-date=March 17, 2026}} He has four older sisters and is a great-grandson of F. Nephi Grigg, a founder of [[Ore-Ida]] and inventor of the [[Tater tots|Tater Tot]].{{Cite news |last=Reynolds |first=Kevin |date=2025-03-20 |title=A BYU basketball player became the face of Tater Tots in March Madness. Here’s why. |url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/byu-cougars/2025/03/20/byus-richie-saunders-is-new-face/ |access-date=2025-03-20 |work=The Salt Lake Tribune |language=en-US}} Saunders attended [[Wasatch Academy]]. Coming out of high school, he was rated as a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was the 3rd ranked prospect from Utah in the class of 2020. He committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]] over offers from [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], [[Utah State Aggies men's basketball|Utah State]], [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]], and [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]].{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |last2=Ireland |first2=Kyle |title=Wasatch Academy’s Richie Saunders Commits To BYU Basketball |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu/richie-saunders-byu-basketball-commits-wasatch-academy/420559 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=13 March 2025}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] in 2022–23, Saunders appeared in 34 games with two starts, averaging 5.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Drew |first1=Jay |title=Richie Saunders is the Renaissance man on BYU’s nationally ranked basketball team |url=https://www.deseret.com/2024/1/24/24046898/byu-cougars-richie-saunders-is-renaissance-man-on-mark-pope-nationally-ranked-basketball-team/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} In 2023–24, he appeared in 34 games with one start and averaged 9.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 1.1 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Weber |first1=Alex |title=BYU guard Richie Saunders enters NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.on3.com/transfer-portal/news/byu-guard-richie-saunders-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal/ |website=On3.com |access-date=13 March 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |title=BYU’s Richie Saunders Announces He Will Enter NCAA Transfer Portal |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu/richie-saunders-byu-basketball-ncaa-transfer-portal/515077 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=13 March 2025}} Saunders entered his name into the [[NCAA transfer portal]] after the season, but ultimately chose to return to play for BYU.{{cite web |last1=Payne |first1=Jackson |title=Why Richie Saunders should be a First Team All-Big 12 selection |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2025/03/03/byu-basketball-richie-saunders-all-big-12-consideration/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} Heading into his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year, he become a full-time starter for the first time in his career.{{cite web |last1=Payne |first1=Jackson |title=BYU’s Egor Demin, Richie Saunders both set to return from injury for the start of Big 12 play |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/12/30/egor-demin-richie-saunders-returning-from-injury-byu-basketball/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} On December 31, 2024, Saunders posted a career-high 30 points in a victory over [[2024–25 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]].{{cite web |last1=Harmon |first1=Dick |title=Veteran Saunders wrecks ASU with career high in BYU’s Big 12 opener |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/12/31/richie-saunders-byu-cougars-arizona-state-basketball-big-12-opener/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} On January 11, 2025, he tallied 26 points in a loss to [[2024–25 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]].{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |title=Kevin Young On BYU’s Richie Saunders: ‘As Talented As Any Wing In The Country’ |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu-basketball/richie-saunders-wing-byu-basketball-kevin-young-talented-country-big-12/535686 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=13 March 2025}} On February 22, Saunders scored 25 points including the pair of game-winning free throws versus [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]].{{cite web |last1=McCann |first1=Dave |title=The ‘S’ in Saunders is for Superman |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2025/02/24/byu-guard-richie-saunders-playing-role-of-super-hero/ |website=Deseret News |access-date=13 March 2025}} For his performance during the 2024–25 season, he was named the Big 12 Most Improved Player while also being named first-team all-Big 12.{{cite web |last1=Harper |first1=Mitch |title=BYU’s Richie Saunders, Egor Demin Earn Big 12 Basketball Awards |url=https://kslsports.com/ncaa/byu-basketball/richie-saunders-award/541446 |website=KSL Sports |access-date=12 March 2025}} On February 15, 2026, Saunders suffered a season-ending [[ACL injury]], essentially ending his collegiate career after playing 25 games in the 2025–26 season.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=BYU star Richie Saunders suffers season-ending torn ACL |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/47941092/byu-star-richie-saunders-suffers-season-ending-torn-acl |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=24 June 2026}} ==Professional career== On June 24, 2026, Saunders was selected with the 32nd overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Richie Saunders is a member of [[the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]]. He served a [[Mormon missionary|mission]] for the church in [[Seattle|Seattle, Washington]]; he was originally called to serve in [[Madagascar]], but was reassigned due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. On September 1, 2023, Saunders married former basketball player Sierra Johnson, who also competed for the [[BYU Cougars women's basketball|BYU Cougars]].{{Cite web |last=Drew |first=Jay |date=January 24, 2024 |title=BYU basketball: This sophomore has been a big reason why the No. 21 Cougars have emerged as a big surprise midway through the 2023-24 season |url=https://www.deseret.com/2024/1/24/24046898/byu-cougars-richie-saunders-is-renaissance-man-on-mark-pope-nationally-ranked-basketball-team/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240124183608/https://www.deseret.com/2024/1/24/24046898/byu-cougars-richie-saunders-is-renaissance-man-on-mark-pope-nationally-ranked-basketball-team/ |archive-date=January 24, 2024 |access-date=June 26, 2026 |website=[[Deseret News]] |language=en}} == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://byucougars.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/player/richie-saunders BYU Cougars bio] {{Memphis Grizzlies current roster}} {{2026 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Saunders, Richie}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Utah]] [[Category:BYU Cougars men's basketball players]] [[Category:Latter Day Saints from Utah]] [[Category:Memphis Grizzlies draft picks]] [[Category:People from Riverton, Utah]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
